title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Any director, officer, key management personnel, executive, contractor, consultant or employee who possesses price-sensitive information about the Company not available to investors and the stock market generally.

tiers.name: Designated Insiders
tiers.description: All Company Directors, the Company Secretary, the Managing Director and CEO, the Chief Operating Officer or equivalent, the Chief Financial Officer or equivalent, all direct reports of the Managing Director and CEO, the Managing Director and CEO and other Executive Directors of wholly owned subsidiaries, all other key management personnel, and any other position nominated by the Chairman.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman personally; distinguished for approval routing (must seek the express permission of the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee to trade outside trading windows, and must advise the Managing Director and CEO).

tiers.name: Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: Distinguished as an approver of trading requests and hardship exemptions for Executives and staff, and as a required co-notifiee of Designated Insiders' dealings.

windows.start_anchor: two (2) week period immediately prior to the release of the Company's half yearly or annual results
windows.end_anchor: three (3) business day period following the release of the half yearly or annual results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairman or the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer may halt trading in the Company securities at any time. Not stated as confidential: an email is sent to the directors, executive management and employees who are affected.

rules.detail: The policy never defines 'Company Securities' beyond the Corporations Act reference and does not mention derivatives, options, warrants or any other derivative product anywhere.
No concept of hedging or limiting economic risk appears anywhere in the policy, for vested or unvested holdings.
Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards are not addressed.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over securities is not mentioned.
Secured financing arrangements generally are not mentioned.
There is no minimum holding period or short-term/speculative dealing rule; only the results-related closed window (section 1.5) restricts timing.

clearance.approver: Chairman and Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (notification); express permission of the Chairman, or in his absence his delegate or the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee, additionally required to trade during a prohibited period
clearance.post_trade_to: Chairman and Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: after the event (no fixed deadline stated)
clearance.evidence: Any Designated Insider is required to notify the Chairman and the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of an intention to trade in securities of the Company, and as applicable, the details of actual trading after the event. The express permission of the Chairman, or in his absence, his delegate or the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee, is required for trading to be conducted during any prohibited period defined by this policy.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board Audit Committee (and must advise the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer)
clearance.post_trade_to: Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
clearance.evidence: The Chairman must seek the express permission of the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for trading to be conducted outside of the trading windows defined by this policy and must also advise the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (for Directors and the Managing Director and CEO) or the Managing Director and CEO or his delegate (for Executives and staff)
exceptions.evidence: there is discretion vested in the Chairman with regard to Directors and the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, or his delegate, with regards to Executives and staff, to allow exemptions to the policy for individuals in special circumstances where application of the policy would cause excessive hardship. However, no such discretion is available if the individual concerned is in actual possession of non-public price sensitive information.

The above restrictions on trading do not restrict participation in any Company share or option plans from time to time but apply in respect of the trading of the Company's shares which participants become entitled to under those plans.

exemption_authority: The Chairman (for Directors and the Managing Director and CEO) or the Managing Director and CEO or his delegate (for Executives and staff) may allow exemptions from the policy for individuals in special circumstances causing excessive hardship, but never while the individual possesses non-public price-sensitive information. Approval must be evidenced in writing (initialled) or by email before trading is instigated, and the Company Secretary retains a record of all exceptions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company's Securities Trading Policy prohibits the buying or selling of Company securities at any time by any director, officer, key management personnel, executive, contractor, consultant or employee ('Insiders') who possesses price-sensitive information about the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy never defines 'Company Securities' to include derivatives, and has no express or dealing-definition-based treatment of hedging, margin lending or secured financing; a funded collar therefore falls into a genuine textual gap rather than being expressly permitted or barred, so company-specific comfort should be sought before relying on silence.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman or the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer may halt trading in the Company securities at any time and an email will be sent to those directors, executive management and employees who are affected.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An ad hoc halt (not stated as confidential, but issued at will) could block execution, roll or unwind of the collar on short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The above restrictions on trading do not restrict participation in any Company share or option plans from time to time but apply in respect of the trading of the Company's shares which participants become entitled to under those plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once plan shares vest, ordinary trading rules (results blackout, notification, insider-information ban) apply to any disposal or hedge of them, but there is no separate express restriction distinguishing unvested from vested holdings for hedging or security purposes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the buying or selling of Company securities at any time by any director, officer, key management personnel, executive, contractor, consultant or employee ('Insiders').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike modern policies, there is no express extension of the notification/approval regime to spouses, family trusts or controlled entities, so on its face routing the collar or loan through such a vehicle may sit outside the policy's clearance mechanics (though general insider trading law would still apply if the individual procures the trade).

summary: This 2010-era policy is largely silent on the mechanics of a funded collar: it contains no definition, express rule or dealing-definition catch-all for derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so neither the put/call legs nor the bank loan secured on the shares are addressed one way or the other. The only substantive constraints are the absolute ban on trading while in possession of price-sensitive information, the closed window running from two weeks before to three business days after half-yearly and annual results, and, for Designated Insiders, notification to the Chairman and Managing Director/CEO of an intention to trade (with express permission required to trade during a prohibited period). A hardship exemption exists but is irrelevant here since there is no underlying prohibition on derivative or financing structures to exempt from. Given this silence, a funded collar is not textually prohibited but also carries interpretive risk; the bank should seek the Company's own confirmation or a comfort letter before proceeding, and in any event should avoid the results blackout window and ensure the Designated Insider notifies the Chairman and CEO of the transaction.
